### New York City campuses

#### Weill Cornell

Main article: [Weill Cornell Medicine](Weill_Cornell_Medicine "Weill Cornell Medicine")

Cornell's medical campus in [New York City](New_York_City "New York City"), also called Weill Cornell, is on the [Upper East Side](Upper_East_Side "Upper East Side") of <Manhattan>. It is home to two Cornell divisions: [Weill Cornell Medical College](Weill_Cornell_Medical_College_of_Cornell_University "Weill Cornell Medical College of Cornell University") and [Weill Cornell Graduate School of Medical Sciences](Weill_Cornell_Graduate_School_of_Medical_Sciences "Weill Cornell Graduate School of Medical Sciences"), and has been affiliated with the [New York-Presbyterian Hospital](NewYork%E2%80%93Presbyterian_Hospital "NewYork–Presbyterian Hospital") since 1927.[[58]](Cornell_University#cite_note-60) Although their faculty and academic divisions are separate, the Medical Center shares administrative and teaching hospital functions with the [Columbia University Medical Center](Columbia_University_Medical_Center "Columbia University Medical Center").[[59]](Cornell_University#cite_note-61) These teaching hospitals include the Payne Whitney Clinic in Manhattan and the Westchester Division in [White Plains, New York](White_Plains%2C_New_York "White Plains, New York").[[60]](Cornell_University#cite_note-62) Weill Cornell Medical College is also affiliated with the neighboring [Memorial Sloan–Kettering Cancer Center](Memorial_Sloan%E2%80%93Kettering_Cancer_Center "Memorial Sloan–Kettering Cancer Center"), [Rockefeller University](Rockefeller_University "Rockefeller University"), and the [Hospital for Special Surgery](Hospital_for_Special_Surgery "Hospital for Special Surgery"). Many faculty members have joint appointments at these institutions. Weill Cornell, Rockefeller, and Memorial Sloan–Kettering offer the [Tri-Institutional MD–PhD Program](Tri-Institutional_MD%E2%80%93PhD_Program "Tri-Institutional MD–PhD Program") to selected entering Cornell medical students.[[61]](Cornell_University#cite_note-63) From 1942 to 1979, the campus also housed the [Cornell School of Nursing](Cornell_School_of_Nursing "Cornell School of Nursing").[[62]](Cornell_University#cite_note-64)

#### Cornell Tech

Main article: [Cornell Tech](Cornell_Tech "Cornell Tech")

On December 19, 2011, Cornell and the [Technion – Israel Institute of Technology](Technion_%E2%80%93_Israel_Institute_of_Technology "Technion – Israel Institute of Technology") won a competition for rights to claim free city land and $100 million in subsidies to build an engineering campus in New York City. The competition was established by New York City Mayor [Michael Bloomberg](Michael_Bloomberg "Michael Bloomberg"), to increase entrepreneurship and job growth in the city's technology sector. The winning bid consisted of a 2.1 million square foot state-of-the-art tech campus to be built on [Roosevelt Island](Roosevelt_Island "Roosevelt Island"), on the site of the former [Coler-Goldwater Specialty Hospital](Coler-Goldwater_Specialty_Hospital "Coler-Goldwater Specialty Hospital"). Instruction began in the fall of 2012, in a temporary location at [111 Eighth Avenue](111_Eighth_Avenue "111 Eighth Avenue") in <Manhattan> in space donated by <Google>.[[63]](Cornell_University#cite_note-65) [Thom Mayne](Thom_Mayne "Thom Mayne"), of the architecture firm <Morphosis>, has been selected to design the first building to be constructed on Roosevelt Island. Begun in 2014, construction of the first phase of the campus was completed in September 2017.[[64]](Cornell_University#cite_note-66)

#### Other New York City programs

In addition to the tech campus and medical center, Cornell maintains local offices in [New York City](New_York_City "New York City") for some of its service programs. The Cornell Urban Scholars Program encourages students to pursue public service careers, arranging assignments with organizations working with New York City's poorest children, families, and communities.[[65]](Cornell_University#cite_note-67) The [NYS College of Human Ecology](Cornell_University_College_of_Human_Ecology "Cornell University College of Human Ecology") and the [NYS College of Agriculture and Life Sciences](Cornell_University_College_of_Agriculture_and_Life_Sciences "Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences") enable students to reach out to local communities by gardening and building with the Cornell Cooperative Extension.[[66]](Cornell_University#cite_note-68) Students with the [NYS School of Industrial and Labor Relations'](Cornell_University_School_of_Industrial_and_Labor_Relations "Cornell University School of Industrial and Labor Relations") Extension and Outreach Program make workplace expertise available to organizations, union members, policymakers, and working adults.[[67]](Cornell_University#cite_note-69) The [College of Engineering's](Cornell_University_College_of_Engineering "Cornell University College of Engineering") Operations Research Manhattan, in the city's [Financial District](Financial_District%2C_Manhattan "Financial District, Manhattan"), brings together business optimization research and decision support services addressed to both financial applications and public health logistics planning.[[68]](Cornell_University#cite_note-70) The [College of Architecture, Art, and Planning](College_of_Architecture%2C_Art%2C_and_Planning "College of Architecture, Art, and Planning") has an 11,000 square foot, <Gensler>-designed facility at [26 Broadway](26_Broadway "26 Broadway") in the [Financial District](Financial_District%2C_Manhattan "Financial District, Manhattan"), that opened in 2015.[[69]](Cornell_University#cite_note-71)

### Qatar campus

Main article: [Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar](Weill_Cornell_Medical_College_in_Qatar "Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar")

[Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar](Weill_Cornell_Medical_College_in_Qatar "Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar") is in [Education City](Education_City%2C_Qatar "Education City, Qatar"), near <Doha>. Opened in September 2004, it was the first American medical school to be established outside of the United States. The college is part of Cornell's program to increase its international influence. The college is a joint initiative with the Qatar government, which seeks to improve the country's academic programs and medical care.[[26]](Cornell_University#cite_note-aboutqatar-28) Along with its full four-year MD program, which mirrors the curriculum taught at [Weill Medical College](Weill_Medical_College "Weill Medical College") in [New York City](New_York_City "New York City"), the college offers a two-year undergraduate [pre-medical](Pre-medical "Pre-medical") program with a separate admissions process. This undergraduate program opened in September 2002 and was the first [coeducational](Coeducation "Coeducation") institute of [higher education](Higher_education "Higher education") in Qatar.[[70]](Cornell_University#cite_note-72)

The college is partially funded by the Qatar government through the [Qatar Foundation](Qatar_Foundation "Qatar Foundation"), which contributed $750 million for its construction.[[71]](Cornell_University#cite_note-73) The medical center is housed in a large two-story structure designed by [Arata Isozaki](Arata_Isozaki "Arata Isozaki"), an internationally known Japanese architect.[[72]](Cornell_University#cite_note-74) In 2004, the Qatar Foundation announced the construction of a 350-bed Specialty Teaching Hospital, near the medical college in Education City. The hospital was to be completed in a few years.[[26]](Cornell_University#cite_note-aboutqatar-28)

### Other facilities

Further information: [Cornell Lab of Ornithology](Cornell_Lab_of_Ornithology "Cornell Lab of Ornithology") and [Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences](Cornell_University_College_of_Agriculture_and_Life_Sciences "Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences")

Cornell University owns and operates a variety of off-campus research facilities and offers study abroad and scholarship programs.[[73]](Cornell_University#cite_note-75) These facilities and programs contribute to the university's research endeavors and provide students with unique learning opportunities.

#### Research facilities

Cornell's off-campus research facilities include Shoals Marine Laboratory, a seasonal marine field station on [Appledore Island](Appledore_Island "Appledore Island") off the <Maine>–[New Hampshire](New_Hampshire "New Hampshire") coast, is operated in conjunction with the [University of New Hampshire](University_of_New_Hampshire "University of New Hampshire") and focuses on undergraduate education and research.[[74]](Cornell_University#cite_note-76) Until 2011, Cornell operated the [Arecibo Observatory](Arecibo_Observatory "Arecibo Observatory") in [Puerto Rico](Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), which was the site of the world's largest single-dish [radio telescope](Radio_telescope "Radio telescope").[[75]](Cornell_University#cite_note-77)

The university also maintains several facilities dedicated to [conservation](Conservation_(ethic) "Conservation (ethic)") and [ecology](Ecology "Ecology"), such as the [New York State Agricultural Experiment Station](New_York_State_Agricultural_Experiment_Station "New York State Agricultural Experiment Station") in [Geneva, New York](Geneva%2C_New_York "Geneva, New York"). Other research facilities include the Animal Science Teaching and Research Center, the Duck Research Laboratory, the Cornell Biological Field Station, the Freeville Organic Research Farm, the Homer C. Thompson Vegetable Research Farm, and biodiversity laboratories in [Punta Cana, Dominican Republic](Punta_Cana%2C_Dominican_Republic "Punta Cana, Dominican Republic"), and the [Peruvian Amazon Rainforest](Peruvian_Amazon_Rainforest "Peruvian Amazon Rainforest").[[80]](Cornell_University#cite_note-82)[[81]](Cornell_University#cite_note-83)[[82]](Cornell_University#cite_note-84)[[83]](Cornell_University#cite_note-85)[[84]](Cornell_University#cite_note-86)[[13]](Cornell_University#cite_note-factbook-14)

Cornell University is a [non-profit organization](Non-profit_organization "Non-profit organization") with a decentralized structure where colleges and schools exercise wide autonomy in defining academic programs, admissions, advising, and conferring degrees. The university comprises nine privately endowed colleges and four publicly supported statutory colleges, offering undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. Cornell operates [eCornell](ECornell "ECornell") for online professional development and certificate programs[[89]](Cornell_University#cite_note-About_eCornell-91) and participates in New York's land-grant, sea-grant, and space-grant programs.[[90]](Cornell_University#cite_note-92)[[91]](Cornell_University#cite_note-93)

Cornell University is governed by a 64-member [board of trustees](Cornell_University_Board_of_Trustees "Cornell University Board of Trustees"), which includes both privately- and publicly-appointed trustees. The board includes trustees appointed by the Governor of New York, alumni-elected trustees, faculty-elected trustees, student-elected trustees,[[92]](Cornell_University#cite_note-94) and non-academic staff-elected trustees. The Governor, [Temporary President of the Senate](Majority_Leader_of_the_New_York_State_Senate "Majority Leader of the New York State Senate"), [Speaker of the Assembly](Speaker_of_the_New_York_State_Assembly "Speaker of the New York State Assembly"), and president of the university serve in an *[ex officio](Ex_officio "Ex officio")* voting capacity. The board is responsible for electing a President to serve as the chief executive and educational officer.[[93]](Cornell_University#cite_note-Bylaws-95)[[94]](Cornell_University#cite_note-96) [Robert Harrison](Robert_Harrison_(financier) "Robert Harrison (financier)") served as the chairman of the board from 2014 to 2022.[[95]](Cornell_University#cite_note-97) The Board of Trustees holds four regular meetings each year, subject to the [New York State Open Meetings Law](Open_Meeting_Law "Open Meeting Law").[[96]](Cornell_University#cite_note-98) Kraig Kayser has served as the chairman of the board since 2022.

## Academics

Cornell is a large, primarily residential research university with a majority of enrollments in undergraduate programs.[[112]](Cornell_University#cite_note-Carnegie-114) The university has been [accredited](Higher_education_accreditation_in_the_United_States "Higher education accreditation in the United States") by the [Middle States Commission on Higher Education](Middle_States_Commission_on_Higher_Education "Middle States Commission on Higher Education") or its predecessor since 1921.[[113]](Cornell_University#cite_note-115) Cornell operates on a 4–1–4 academic calendar with the fall term beginning in late August and ending in early December, a three-week winter session in January, and the spring term beginning in late January and ending in early May.[[114]](Cornell_University#cite_note-116)

Cornell, along with [Oregon State University](Oregon_State_University "Oregon State University"), [Pennsylvania State University](Pennsylvania_State_University "Pennsylvania State University"), [University of Georgia](University_of_Georgia "University of Georgia"), and [University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa](University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_at_M%C4%81noa "University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa"), are the only institutions to be [land-grant universities](Land-grant_university "Land-grant university") that are also members of the other three "grant" programs: [sea grant](National_Sea_Grant_College_Program "National Sea Grant College Program"), [space grant](National_Space_Grant_College_and_Fellowship_Program "National Space Grant College and Fellowship Program"), and [sun grant](Sun_grant_colleges "Sun grant colleges"). Admission to Cornell University is highly competitive. In spring of 2022 (Class of 2026), Cornell's undergraduate programs received 71,164 applications and admitted only 5,168 for a 7.2% acceptance rate.[[116]](Cornell_University#cite_note-118) For Fall 2019 enrolling freshmen, the middle 50% range of <SAT> scores were 680–760 for evidence-based reading and writing and 720–800 for mathematics.[[117]](Cornell_University#cite_note-CDS-119) The middle 50% range of the [ACT](ACT_(test) "ACT (test)") composite score was 32–35.[[117]](Cornell_University#cite_note-CDS-119)

The university continues to attract a diverse and inclusive student body. The proportion of admitted students who self-identify as underrepresented minorities increased to 34.2% from 33.7% in 2021, and 59.3% self-identify as students of color. That number has increased steadily over the past five years, enrollment officials said, from 52.5% in 2017 and 57.2% in 2020.

Of those admitted, 1,163 will be first-generation college students, another increase over 2020's 844.[[118]](Cornell_University#cite_note-120) The university is [need-blind](Need-blind "Need-blind") for domestic applicants.[[119]](Cornell_University#cite_note-121)

### Financial aid

Cornell University, under Section 9 of its original charter, ensures equal access to education by admitting students without distinction based on rank, class, occupation, or locality.[[120]](Cornell_University#cite_note-charter-122) The charter also mandates free instruction for one student from each Assembly district in the state.[[120]](Cornell_University#cite_note-charter-122)

From the 1950s to the 1980s, Cornell collaborated with other [Ivy League](Ivy_League "Ivy League") institutions to establish a uniform [financial aid](Student_financial_aid "Student financial aid") system.[[121]](Cornell_University#cite_note-2005-06_Financial_Plan-123) Although a 1989 consent decree ended this collaboration due to an antitrust investigation, all Ivy League schools still offer need-based financial aid without athletic scholarships.[[122]](Cornell_University#cite_note-124) In December 2010, Cornell pledged to match any grant component of financial aid offers from other Ivy League schools, <MIT>, [Duke](Duke_University "Duke University"), or [Stanford](Stanford_University "Stanford University") for accepted applicants considering these institutions.[[123]](Cornell_University#cite_note-125)

In 2008, Cornell introduced a financial aid initiative, gradually replacing need-based loans with scholarships for undergraduate students from lower-income families.[[124]](Cornell_University#cite_note-126) Despite a 27% drop in the university's endowment in 2008, the then-president allocated additional funds to continue the initiative, seeking to raise $125 million in donations for its support.[[125]](Cornell_University#cite_note-127) By 2010, Cornell successfully met the full financial aid needs of 40% of full-time freshmen with financial need, and the average undergraduate student debt upon graduation was $21,549.[[126]](Cornell_University#cite_note-fa-128)

### 19th century

Cornell University was founded on April 27, 1865 by [Ezra Cornell](Ezra_Cornell "Ezra Cornell"), an entrepreneur and New York State Senator, and [Andrew Dickson White](Andrew_Dickson_White "Andrew Dickson White"), an educator and fellow New York State Senator, after the [New York State legislature](New_York_State "New York State") authorized the university as the state's [land grant](Land-grant_university "Land-grant university") institution.[[16]](Cornell_University#cite_note-17) Ezra Cornell offered his farm in [Ithaca, New York](Ithaca%2C_New_York "Ithaca, New York") as a preliminary site for the university along with $500,000 of his personal fortune as an initial [endowment](Financial_endowment "Financial endowment") (equivalent to $11,884,000 in 2022), and White agreed to be Cornell University's first president.

During Cornell University's first three years, White oversaw the construction of the first two buildings and traveled to attract students and [faculty](Faculty_(university) "Faculty (university)").[[17]](Cornell_University#cite_note-founding-18) The university was inaugurated on October 7, 1868, and 412 men were enrolled the next day.[[18]](Cornell_University#cite_note-opening-19)

Cornell developed as a technologically innovative institution, applying its research to its own campus and to outreach efforts. In 1883, it was one of the first university campuses to use electricity from a water-powered [dynamo](Dynamo "Dynamo") to light the campus grounds.[[19]](Cornell_University#cite_note-chp-20) Since 1894, Cornell has included colleges that are state funded and fulfill statutory requirements;[[20]](Cornell_University#cite_note-21) it has also administered research and extension activities that have been jointly funded by New York state along with [federal government](Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States") matching programs.[[21]](Cornell_University#cite_note-22)

Cornell has had active alumni since its earliest classes. It was one of the first universities to include alumni-elected representatives on its board of trustees.[[lower-alpha 2]](Cornell_University#cite_note-26)

Cornell is home to the [Cornell University Press](Cornell_University_Press "Cornell University Press"), founded in 1869, the country's oldest publishing enterprise. Cornell was first home to the Cornell Era, a weekly campus publication founded in 1868. But the [Cornell Daily Sun](Cornell_Daily_Sun "Cornell Daily Sun"), an independent student-run newspaper founded in 1880 became the school's leading publication. Today, the Sun is the oldest continuously independent college daily in the United States.

In the 19th century, Cornell was also home to numerous [literary societies](Cornell_literary_societies "Cornell literary societies"), founded to encourage writing, reading, and oration skills. The U.S. Bureau of Education described three of them as a "purely literary society" following the "traditions of the old literary societies of Eastern universities. These societies largely disappeared by the 20th century.

### 20th century

Cornell was among the [Ivies](Ivy_League "Ivy League") that experienced heightened student activism during the 1960s, related to cultural issues, civil rights, and opposition to the [Vietnam War](Vietnam_War "Vietnam War"). Protests and occupations resulted in the resignation of Cornell's president and the restructuring of university governance.[[25]](Cornell_University#cite_note-Downs1999-27)

In 1967, Cornell experienced a fire in the Residential Club dormitory that killed eight students and one professor.

Central Campus is the heart of the university, housing the majority of academic and administrative facilities. These Collegiate Gothic structures add a sense of historical charm to the campus, while the modern residence halls provide comfortable accommodations for students."[[45]](Cornell_University#cite_note-47)

In the nearby [Collegetown](College_town "College town") neighborhood, the architectural styles are more diverse, reflecting the area's mixed-use nature. The Schwartz Performing Arts Center and two upper-level residence halls[[46]](Cornell_University#cite_note-48)[[47]](Cornell_University#cite_note-49) are surrounded by a variety of apartment buildings, eateries, and businesses, creating a vibrant and lively atmosphere for students and residents alike.[[48]](Cornell_University#cite_note-50)

#### Natural surroundings

The Ithaca campus is located in the [Finger Lakes](Finger_Lakes "Finger Lakes") region and has views of the [city](Ithaca%2C_New_York "Ithaca, New York"), [Cayuga Lake](Cayuga_Lake "Cayuga Lake"), and the surrounding valleys. The campus is bordered by two [gorges](Gorge "Gorge"), Fall Creek Gorge and Cascadilla Gorge, which contribute to the university's natural landscape. Although these gorges are popular swimming spots during warmer months, their use is discouraged by the university and city code due to potential safety hazards.[[49]](Cornell_University#cite_note-51) Adjacent to the main campus, Cornell owns the 2,800-acre (1,100 ha) [Cornell Botanic Gardens](Cornell_Botanic_Gardens "Cornell Botanic Gardens"), featuring various plants, trees, and ponds. The gardens' trails allow visitors to explore the natural surroundings.[[50]](Cornell_University#cite_note-52)

#### Sustainability

Cornell University has implemented various [green initiatives](Greening "Greening") to promote sustainability and reduce its environmental impact. Key projects include a gas-fired combined heat and power facility,[[51]](Cornell_University#cite_note-53) an on-campus hydroelectric plant,[[52]](Cornell_University#cite_note-54) and a [lake source cooling](Deep_lake_water_cooling "Deep lake water cooling") system.[[53]](Cornell_University#cite_note-55) In 2007, Cornell established a Center for a Sustainable Future.[[54]](Cornell_University#cite_note-56) The university has committed to achieving net carbon neutrality by 2035[[55]](Cornell_University#cite_note-:02-57) and, as of 2020, is powered by six solar farms providing a total of 28 megawatts of power.[[56]](Cornell_University#cite_note-58) Additionally, Cornell is developing an enhanced geothermal system, Earth Source Heating, to meet campus heating needs.[[57]](Cornell_University#cite_note-59)

### New York City campuses

#### Weill Cornell

Main article: [Weill Cornell Medicine](Weill_Cornell_Medicine "Weill Cornell Medicine")

Cornell's medical campus in [New York City](New_York_City "New York City"), also called Weill Cornell, is on the [Upper East Side](Upper_East_Side "Upper East Side") of <Manhattan>. It is home to two Cornell divisions: [Weill Cornell Medical College](Weill_Cornell_Medical_College_of_Cornell_University "Weill Cornell Medical College of Cornell University") and [Weill Cornell Graduate School of Medical Sciences](Weill_Cornell_Graduate_School_of_Medical_Sciences "Weill Cornell Graduate School of Medical Sciences"), and has been affiliated with the [New York-Presbyterian Hospital](NewYork%E2%80%93Presbyterian_Hospital "NewYork–Presbyterian Hospital") since 1927.[[58]](Cornell_University#cite_note-60) Although their faculty and academic divisions are separate, the Medical Center shares administrative and teaching hospital functions with the [Columbia University Medical Center](Columbia_University_Medical_Center "Columbia University Medical Center").[[59]](Cornell_University#cite_note-61) These teaching hospitals include the Payne Whitney Clinic in Manhattan and the Westchester Division in [White Plains, New York](White_Plains%2C_New_York "White Plains, New York").[[60]](Cornell_University#cite_note-62) Weill Cornell Medical College is also affiliated with the neighboring [Memorial Sloan–Kettering Cancer Center](Memorial_Sloan%E2%80%93Kettering_Cancer_Center "Memorial Sloan–Kettering Cancer Center"), [Rockefeller University](Rockefeller_University "Rockefeller University"), and the [Hospital for Special Surgery](Hospital_for_Special_Surgery "Hospital for Special Surgery"). Many faculty members have joint appointments at these institutions. Weill Cornell, Rockefeller, and Memorial Sloan–Kettering offer the [Tri-Institutional MD–PhD Program](Tri-Institutional_MD%E2%80%93PhD_Program "Tri-Institutional MD–PhD Program") to selected entering Cornell medical students.[[61]](Cornell_University#cite_note-63) From 1942 to 1979, the campus also housed the [Cornell School of Nursing](Cornell_School_of_Nursing "Cornell School of Nursing").[[62]](Cornell_University#cite_note-64)

#### Cornell Tech

Main article: [Cornell Tech](Cornell_Tech "Cornell Tech")

On December 19, 2011, Cornell and the [Technion – Israel Institute of Technology](Technion_%E2%80%93_Israel_Institute_of_Technology "Technion – Israel Institute of Technology") won a competition for rights to claim free city land and $100 million in subsidies to build an engineering campus in New York City. The competition was established by New York City Mayor [Michael Bloomberg](Michael_Bloomberg "Michael Bloomberg"), to increase entrepreneurship and job growth in the city's technology sector. The winning bid consisted of a 2.1 million square foot state-of-the-art tech campus to be built on [Roosevelt Island](Roosevelt_Island "Roosevelt Island"), on the site of the former [Coler-Goldwater Specialty Hospital](Coler-Goldwater_Specialty_Hospital "Coler-Goldwater Specialty Hospital"). Instruction began in the fall of 2012, in a temporary location at [111 Eighth Avenue](111_Eighth_Avenue "111 Eighth Avenue") in <Manhattan> in space donated by <Google>.[[63]](Cornell_University#cite_note-65) [Thom Mayne](Thom_Mayne "Thom Mayne"), of the architecture firm <Morphosis>, has been selected to design the first building to be constructed on Roosevelt Island. Begun in 2014, construction of the first phase of the campus was completed in September 2017.[[64]](Cornell_University#cite_note-66)

#### Other New York City programs

In addition to the tech campus and medical center, Cornell maintains local offices in [New York City](New_York_City "New York City") for some of its service programs. The Cornell Urban Scholars Program encourages students to pursue public service careers, arranging assignments with organizations working with New York City's poorest children, families, and communities.[[65]](Cornell_University#cite_note-67) The [NYS College of Human Ecology](Cornell_University_College_of_Human_Ecology "Cornell University College of Human Ecology") and the [NYS College of Agriculture and Life Sciences](Cornell_University_College_of_Agriculture_and_Life_Sciences "Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences") enable students to reach out to local communities by gardening and building with the Cornell Cooperative Extension.[[66]](Cornell_University#cite_note-68) Students with the [NYS School of Industrial and Labor Relations'](Cornell_University_School_of_Industrial_and_Labor_Relations "Cornell University School of Industrial and Labor Relations") Extension and Outreach Program make workplace expertise available to organizations, union members, policymakers, and working adults.[[67]](Cornell_University#cite_note-69) The [College of Engineering's](Cornell_University_College_of_Engineering "Cornell University College of Engineering") Operations Research Manhattan, in the city's [Financial District](Financial_District%2C_Manhattan "Financial District, Manhattan"), brings together business optimization research and decision support services addressed to both financial applications and public health logistics planning.[[68]](Cornell_University#cite_note-70) The [College of Architecture, Art, and Planning](College_of_Architecture%2C_Art%2C_and_Planning "College of Architecture, Art, and Planning") has an 11,000 square foot, <Gensler>-designed facility at [26 Broadway](26_Broadway "26 Broadway") in the [Financial District](Financial_District%2C_Manhattan "Financial District, Manhattan"), that opened in 2015.[[69]](Cornell_University#cite_note-71)

### Qatar campus

Main article: [Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar](Weill_Cornell_Medical_College_in_Qatar "Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar")

[Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar](Weill_Cornell_Medical_College_in_Qatar "Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar") is in [Education City](Education_City%2C_Qatar "Education City, Qatar"), near <Doha>. Opened in September 2004, it was the first American medical school to be established outside of the United States. The college is part of Cornell's program to increase its international influence. The college is a joint initiative with the Qatar government, which seeks to improve the country's academic programs and medical care.[[26]](Cornell_University#cite_note-aboutqatar-28) Along with its full four-year MD program, which mirrors the curriculum taught at [Weill Medical College](Weill_Medical_College "Weill Medical College") in [New York City](New_York_City "New York City"), the college offers a two-year undergraduate [pre-medical](Pre-medical "Pre-medical") program with a separate admissions process. This undergraduate program opened in September 2002 and was the first [coeducational](Coeducation "Coeducation") institute of [higher education](Higher_education "Higher education") in Qatar.[[70]](Cornell_University#cite_note-72)

The college is partially funded by the Qatar government through the [Qatar Foundation](Qatar_Foundation "Qatar Foundation"), which contributed $750 million for its construction.[[71]](Cornell_University#cite_note-73) The medical center is housed in a large two-story structure designed by [Arata Isozaki](Arata_Isozaki "Arata Isozaki"), an internationally known Japanese architect.[[72]](Cornell_University#cite_note-74) In 2004, the Qatar Foundation announced the construction of a 350-bed Specialty Teaching Hospital, near the medical college in Education City. The hospital was to be completed in a few years.[[26]](Cornell_University#cite_note-aboutqatar-28)

### Other facilities

Further information: [Cornell Lab of Ornithology](Cornell_Lab_of_Ornithology "Cornell Lab of Ornithology") and [Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences](Cornell_University_College_of_Agriculture_and_Life_Sciences "Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences")

Cornell University owns and operates a variety of off-campus research facilities and offers study abroad and scholarship programs.[[73]](Cornell_University#cite_note-75) These facilities and programs contribute to the university's research endeavors and provide students with unique learning opportunities.

#### Research facilities

Cornell's off-campus research facilities include Shoals Marine Laboratory, a seasonal marine field station on [Appledore Island](Appledore_Island "Appledore Island") off the <Maine>–[New Hampshire](New_Hampshire "New Hampshire") coast, is operated in conjunction with the [University of New Hampshire](University_of_New_Hampshire "University of New Hampshire") and focuses on undergraduate education and research.[[74]](Cornell_University#cite_note-76) Until 2011, Cornell operated the [Arecibo Observatory](Arecibo_Observatory "Arecibo Observatory") in [Puerto Rico](Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), which was the site of the world's largest single-dish [radio telescope](Radio_telescope "Radio telescope").[[75]](Cornell_University#cite_note-77)

The university also maintains several facilities dedicated to [conservation](Conservation_(ethic) "Conservation (ethic)") and [ecology](Ecology "Ecology"), such as the [New York State Agricultural Experiment Station](New_York_State_Agricultural_Experiment_Station "New York State Agricultural Experiment Station") in [Geneva, New York](Geneva%2C_New_York "Geneva, New York"). This station operates three substations, including the Cornell Lake Erie Research and Extension Laboratory in [Portland](Portland%2C_New_York "Portland, New York"),[[76]](Cornell_University#cite_note-78) the Hudson Valley Laboratory in [Highland](Highland%2C_Ulster_County%2C_New_York "Highland, Ulster County, New York"),[[77]](Cornell_University#cite_note-79) and the Long Island Horticultural Research Laboratory in [Riverhead](Riverhead_(town)%2C_New_York "Riverhead (town), New York").[[78]](Cornell_University#cite_note-80) The [Cornell Lab of Ornithology](Cornell_Lab_of_Ornithology "Cornell Lab of Ornithology") in Ithaca conducts research on [biological diversity](Biodiversity "Biodiversity"), primarily in birds,[[79]](Cornell_University#cite_note-81)

Other research facilities include the Animal Science Teaching and Research Center, the Duck Research Laboratory, the Cornell Biological Field Station, the Freeville Organic Research Farm, the Homer C. Thompson Vegetable Research Farm, and biodiversity laboratories in [Punta Cana, Dominican Republic](Punta_Cana%2C_Dominican_Republic "Punta Cana, Dominican Republic"), and the [Peruvian Amazon Rainforest](Peruvian_Amazon_Rainforest "Peruvian Amazon Rainforest").[[80]](Cornell_University#cite_note-82)[[81]](Cornell_University#cite_note-83)[[82]](Cornell_University#cite_note-84)[[83]](Cornell_University#cite_note-85)[[84]](Cornell_University#cite_note-86)[[13]](Cornell_University#cite_note-factbook-14)

#### Study abroad and scholarship programs

Cornell offers various [study abroad](Study_abroad "Study abroad") and [scholarship](Scholarship "Scholarship") programs that allow students to gain experience and earn credit towards their degrees. The "Capital Semester" program offers students the opportunity to intern in the [New York State Legislature](New_York_State_Legislature "New York State Legislature") in Albany. The Cornell in Washington program enables students to spend a semester in [Washington, D.C.](Washington%2C_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), participating in research or internships.[[85]](Cornell_University#cite_note-87) Similarly, the Cornell in Rome program, allows students to study architecture, urban studies, and the arts in [Rome, Italy](Rome%2C_Italy "Rome, Italy").[[86]](Cornell_University#cite_note-88)

#### Cooperative extension service

As New York State's [land-grant university](Land-grant_university "Land-grant university"), Cornell operates a [cooperative extension service](Cooperative_extension_service "Cooperative extension service") with 56 offices spread across the state. These offices provide programs in agriculture and food systems, children, youth and families, community and economic vitality, environment and natural resources, and nutrition and health.[[87]](Cornell_University#cite_note-89) Additionally, the university operates New York's Animal Health Diagnostic Center, which serves as a valuable resource for animal disease control and husbandry.[[88]](Cornell_University#cite_note-90)

> *Denique (quid verbis opus est?) spectemur agendo!*

content:
Based on my search through the Wikipedia article "List of university and college mottos," I found Cornell University's entry. However, there's an important finding: **Cornell University does not have a traditional Latin motto** like many other universities. Instead, its motto is actually a famous quote by founder Ezra Cornell, which is in English.

Here's the information from the table:

**Full Row from the Table:**

| University | Motto | Language | Translation |
|------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| [Cornell University](Cornell_University "Cornell University") | I would found an institution where any person can find instruction in any study – [Ezra Cornell](Ezra_Cornell "Ezra Cornell"), 1865 | English | *(empty)* |

**Key Findings:**
- **Latin Motto**: Cornell University does not have a formal Latin motto in the Wikipedia list
- **English Motto**: "I would found an institution where any person can find instruction in any study"
- **Language**: English (not Latin)
- **Translation**: N/A (the motto is already in English)

This reflects Ezra Cornell's vision from 1865 when he founded the university - a democratic educational institution accessible to "any person" in "any study." This philosophy, rather than a traditional Latin motto, serves as Cornell's official motto and represents the university's founding ideals.
